architecture-2025.title: Web Architecture in 2025: Key Trends
architecture-2025.excerpt: An overview of modern architectures for high-performance applications.
architecture-2025.author: Yoann Andrieux
content: Web architecture constantly evolves to meet the demands of performance, scalability, and user experience. In 2025, several trends clearly stand out.
Serverless and edge-first architectures continue to gain ground. Deploying code closer to users drastically reduces latency and improves the overall experience.
The Islands Architecture paradigm, popularized by Astro, optimizes JavaScript sent to the client by only making interactive the components that need it.
React Server Components are transforming our approach to server-side rendering, allowing content streaming while maintaining a smooth user experience.
Finally, the adoption of edge databases like Turso or PlanetScale brings data closer to users, completing a truly distributed architecture.

saas-vs-custom.title: SaaS vs Custom: How to Choose?
saas-vs-custom.excerpt: Criteria for deciding between an existing solution and custom development.
saas-vs-custom.author: Yoann Andrieux
content: Choosing between a SaaS solution and custom development is a strategic decision that impacts your company's long-term future.
SaaS offers quick implementation and reduced initial cost. It's ideal for validating a concept or when the need exactly matches what the market offers.
Custom development, on the other hand, allows perfect adaptation to your business processes and strong competitive differentiation. It's an investment that makes sense when your workflow is unique.
Key criteria to consider: the level of customization required, total budget over 3-5 years, strategic importance of the project, and your ability to maintain a custom solution.
In many cases, a hybrid approach is relevant: use SaaS for commoditized functions and develop custom where you create value.

ux-errors.title: 5 UX Mistakes That Kill Your Conversions
ux-errors.excerpt: Analysis of the most common problems and how to solve them.
ux-errors.author: Yoann Andrieux
content: Good UX isn't a luxury, it's a conversion lever. Here are the most common mistakes we encounter in audits.
Mistake #1: Forms that are too long. Each additional field reduces your conversion rate. Only ask for essentials at each step.
Mistake #2: Invisible or confusing CTAs. Your main action button should be obvious and its label explicit about what will happen.
Mistake #3: Cognitive overload. Too many options, too much text, too many distractions. Simplify and guide the user toward their goal.
Mistake #4: Lack of feedback. Users should always know where they are: loading, success, error. Silence is anxiety-inducing.
Mistake #5: Ignoring mobile. More than half of traffic is mobile. If the experience isn't flawless on small screens, you're losing customers.

mvp-iteration.title: MVP and Iteration: The Right Approach
mvp-iteration.excerpt: How to build an effective minimum viable product and iterate intelligently.
mvp-iteration.author: Yoann Andrieux
content: The MVP concept is often misunderstood. It's not about delivering a sloppy product, but creating the simplest version that validates a hypothesis.
The key is identifying the core value of your product. What makes it unique and essential? This is the core feature the MVP should focus on.
Define clear metrics before launching. Without success criteria, you won't know how to interpret results and decide what's next.
Iteration should be fast and data-driven. Analyze user behaviors, gather qualitative feedback, and prioritize ruthlessly.
Don't be afraid to pivot if the data suggests it. An MVP that fails isn't a failure, it's valuable learning that brings you closer to product-market fit.

core-web-vitals.title: Core Web Vitals: A Practical Guide
core-web-vitals.excerpt: Everything about web performance metrics and how to optimize them.
core-web-vitals.author: Yoann Andrieux
content: Core Web Vitals have become a Google ranking factor. But beyond SEO, they reflect user experience quality.
LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) measures perceived loading time. Goal: under 2.5 seconds. Optimize your images, use lazy loading, and preload critical resources.
FID (First Input Delay) measures responsiveness. Goal: under 100ms. Reduce blocking JavaScript and use code splitting.
CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) measures visual stability. Goal: under 0.1. Reserve space for images and avoid dynamic content injections.
Essential tools: Lighthouse for auditing, WebPageTest for detailed diagnostics, and Chrome DevTools for debugging. Measure in real conditions, not just locally.
Optimization is an ongoing process. Integrate performance tests into your CI/CD and monitor regressions.

owasp-2024.title: Web Security: OWASP Top 10 in Practice
owasp-2024.excerpt: The most common vulnerabilities and how to protect your applications.
owasp-2024.author: Yoann Andrieux
content: Security is not optional. The OWASP Top 10 lists the most critical vulnerabilities every developer should know.
Injections (SQL, NoSQL, LDAP) remain at the top. Always use parameterized queries and rigorously validate user input.
Broken authentication is a classic. Implement 2FA, use proven libraries, and never reinvent the wheel with passwords.
Sensitive data exposure can be fatal. Encrypt in transit (HTTPS) and at rest, minimize stored data, and regularly audit your endpoints.
Vulnerable components are an often-neglected risk. Keep your dependencies up to date, use automated audit tools like Snyk or Dependabot.
Security is everyone's business. Train your teams, integrate security tests into your pipeline, and have critical applications audited by experts.
